items.prose: A call option with strike £50.00 pays the final price minus £50.00 when the price is above £50.00, and nothing otherwise. The final price can be any amount from £0.00 up.
items.question: What is the range of the payoff?

options.why: You capped it at the strike. Above £50.00 the payoff keeps rising with the price.
You read the right end of the chart. The price can go above £100.00, and the payoff with it.
£50.00 is the strike, an input. Below it the payoff is £0.00.

feedback.correct: The payoff is £0.00 up to the strike, then rises without limit.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Read the heights of the line, not the prices along the bottom.

explain.text: Below £50.00 the payoff is £0.00, so 0 is in the range. Above it the payoff is $S - 50$, which grows with no top. So the range is payoff $\ge 0$.

items.question: Which fee schedule gives every trade size exactly one fee?

A trade of exactly £2,000.00 is in neither band, so it gets no fee.

explain.text: "Below" leaves £2,000.00 out of the first band, and "from £2,000.00 up" puts it in the second. So every trade size, the boundary included, has one fee.
